approval_notes: Orchestrator-directed F007 Slice 1: LLM provider abstraction + routing ladder + natural-language intake + per-request ephemeral consent + deterministic fallback (backend + a thin web NL/consent UI). Build ONE slice, open ONE PR, do NOT merge, do NOT flip any passes flag. F007 stays passes:false.

The LLM's ONLY job is free text -> a candidate structured requirements object that is validated through the EXISTING app.adviser.schema.RecommendationRequest (extra=forbid, bounds, _reject_url_like, exact-Decimal) and passed to the EXISTING recommend(). The LLM path NEVER re-derives Z0/quota/classification. Deterministic fallback is ALWAYS retained.

Owner decisions: Q1=A a deterministic FAKE/echo adapter is the only adapter exercised in CI (the offline suite); all 4 real providers stay enabled:false, thin, config-gated, and are NEVER invoked (no network in CI/live-smoke). Q2=A consent is per-request EPHEMERAL, not persisted server-side, prompts/descriptions never logged, consent re-asked each session. Q7=A one combined slice (backend + thin web NL textarea + consent modal). Q9=A no new runtime dependency (FastAPI + Python stdlib only).
objective: Add an LLM-assisted natural-language intake to the adviser that turns free text into a candidate structured RecommendationRequest via a routing ladder (deterministic parser -> local model -> free hosted with consent -> commercial escalation -> deterministic fallback), validates any candidate through the existing strict schema (fail-closed), and passes a valid interpretation to the existing deterministic recommend(). External providers require an explicit per-request consent assertion (ephemeral, never persisted, never logged); without it external tiers are skipped. Timeout/provider-error/malformed-output/consent-absent all degrade gracefully to the next tier and ultimately to a deterministic fallback that never hard-fails the user's task. Add a thin web NL textarea (bounded to maximum_input_characters) + a consent modal to #/adviser, rendering the interpretation, routing info (llm_used, fallback_reason), and the deterministic recommendation via the existing RecommendationView. No migration; Alembic head stays 0007.

acceptance_criteria: 1. A new POST /adviser/recommend/assisted endpoint accepts a structured AssistedRequest (free-text description + optional ephemeral consent), runs the routing ladder, validates any candidate interpretation through the EXISTING RecommendationRequest (extra=forbid, bounds, _reject_url_like, exact-Decimal), and — when valid — returns the EXISTING deterministic recommendation plus routing metadata (llm_used, llm_provider, routing_path, fallback_reason). GET -> 405.

2. Deterministic fallback is always retained: with ALL providers disabled, a description the deterministic parser handles yields llm_used=false and a recommendation byte-identical to POST /adviser/recommend for the equivalent structured requirements; a description nothing can interpret returns a graceful deterministic response (interpreted=false, fallback_reason set, no hard failure).

3. Routing precedence is proven: deterministic parser first (no LLM, no consent); then local; then free-hosted (consent-gated); then commercial (consent-gated); then deterministic fallback. An external tier is SKIPPED when consent is absent, and the request still returns a deterministic result.

4. Failure handling degrades, never hard-fails: an LLM timeout, an LLM provider error, and malformed LLM output rejected by the strict schema each fall through to the next tier and ultimately to the deterministic fallback with a clear fallback_reason (proven with the fake adapter).

5. Consent is enforced at the routing boundary, ephemeral, and never logged: external providers require an explicit per-request consent assertion; the description/prompt is never written to logs or persisted; consent is not stored server-side.

6. Security posture: the LLM has ONLY the interpret capability (no credentials, filesystem, shell, URL-fetch, admin, or publication); secrets are referenced by env-var name only; the public NL endpoint takes no user-controlled URL (reject_urls -> 422) and enforces maximum_input_characters (over-limit -> 422); provider base_url comes from config and is passed through the reused SSRF scheme guard.
7. The no-LLM-import guard on the deterministic core stays intact: importing app.adviser.recommend/select/schema/schemas does NOT import app.adviser.llm (subprocess-asserted).

8. Web: #/adviser offers an accessible Structured|Assisted mode switch; the assisted mode has a bounded NL textarea (maximum_input_characters) and a consent modal that identifies the external provider/model, warns against secrets/PII, explains external processing, links the provider policy (rel=noopener noreferrer), and requires explicit opt-in; results render the interpretation + routing notice + the existing RecommendationView; honest 'couldn't interpret' when interpretation is null; the UI never re-derives Z0/confidence/quota math.

9. No new npm/Python dependency and no migration: Alembic head stays 0007; requirements-sync + npm audit + detect-secrets stay green; existing F006/earlier backend tests stay green (only additive tests + the additive router import).

10. Offline gates green: scripts/test.ps1 exit 0 (pytest incl. the new routing/parser/runtime/consent/fallback/no-import tests + web vitest incl. the assisted UI + vite build) and scripts/check.ps1 -NodeAudit exit 0 (all 8 gates).

11. Live (alt ports, isolated compose project ftatlas_s1, ALL providers disabled): fresh stack (head 0007) + smoke; POST the assisted endpoint direct :8010 AND via nginx /api :8090 proving it degrades to deterministic output (llm_used=false, fallback_reason set) identical to POST /adviser/recommend; consent-absent still returns a deterministic result; GET->405; URL-in-body->422; a headless jsdom render of the REAL <App/> at #/adviser assisted mode against the live proxy.
12. F007 remains passes:false; a fresh-context independent Level 2 evaluator owns any status change. Did NOT merge.

risks.data_migration: None: consent is ephemeral and not persisted. No migration; Alembic head stays 0007; no new table; the assisted endpoint is stateless and read-only (SELECT only via the existing gather_candidates).
risks.security_privacy: The NL description is never logged or persisted. The public endpoint takes no user-controlled URL (reject_urls -> 422) and bounds input length (maximum_input_characters -> 422). External providers require an explicit ephemeral consent assertion at the routing boundary. The LLM has only the interpret capability — no credentials, filesystem, shell, URL-fetch, admin, or publication. Provider base_url comes from config and is passed through the reused SSRF scheme guard; the 4 real adapters do no network in this slice (raise on interpret). Secrets are env-var-name-only; detect-secrets stays green.
risks.portability: No new npm or Python runtime dependency (FastAPI + Python stdlib only). amd64/arm64 unaffected. Provider-specific logic is hidden behind the LlmProvider Protocol + config-gated adapters.
risks.zero_cost_safety: The LLM path NEVER re-derives Z0/quota/classification: it only proposes a candidate structured RecommendationRequest, which is validated by the existing strict schema and fed to the existing deterministic recommend(). Deterministic fallback is always retained and proven byte-identical with LLM disabled. No LLM-to-publication path. Honest 'couldn't interpret' when nothing parseable.
risks.immutability: No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and no schema change; the deterministic adviser core is untouched (additive router import only); immutability/separation triggers unaffected.
risks.regression: Additive: a new llm/ package + assist_schema + one new endpoint + one settings field + an additive compose mount + additive web types/fetcher/component/mode-switch + additive tests. The existing POST /adviser/recommend, the deterministic core, the catalogue views, and all existing tests are unchanged.
risks.supply_chain: No new npm or Python dependency; requirements-sync + npm audit + pip-audit stay green; already-present deps only.
